definition: Modular Audio Recognition Framework (MARF) is an open-source research platform and a collection of voice, sound, speech, text and natural language processing (NLP) algorithms written in Java and arranged into a modular and extensible framework that attempts to facilitate addition of new algorithms.
details: MARF may act as a library in applications or be used as a source for learning and extension. A few example applications are provided to show how to use the framework. There is also a detailed manual and the API reference in the javadoc format as the project tends to be well documented. MARF, its applications, and the corresponding source code and documentation are released under the BSD-style license.

explainer.lead: MARF is an open-source Java platform collecting voice, sound, speech, text and NLP algorithms in a modular, extensible design. It matters as a documented base for research and for adding new algorithms without rebuilding the system.

tiers.eli5: Think of a toolbox where each tool does one sound or language job, and you can drop in your own tool whenever you need one.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as a library inside applications or as reference source for learning and extension, with sample applications, a manual and javadoc API docs provided. A pitfall is treating it as production-ready: it is a research platform released under a BSD-style license.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, MARF is a modular framework of audio, speech, text and NLP algorithm implementations in Java, extensible by adding new algorithm modules; the documentation does not specify performance bounds, so limits are not stated.

explainer.example: A developer wanting speech-processing capability can embed MARF as a library in a Java application, or study its bundled example applications to see how the framework is wired.
